findings.finding: On 2026-08-18 BARDA awarded Modification No. 21 to the CYFENDUS anthrax vaccine contract, worth about $24M, after the Aug 5 guide was set. The Sep 14 IR deck lists it as 'new in Q3'. If delivered in Q3 it is about 20% of the $110-130M Q3 revenue guide and could push revenue above the $123M consensus; the release gives no delivery quarter and does not say whether it was in guidance.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Prints driven by MCM contract timing have moved this stock hard both ways: Q2 2026 (accelerated MCM, with a guide cut) -29.6%; Q3 2025 +36.6%; Q2 2025 +36.7% (baseline history). The quarter's MCM revenue line has historically decided the sign together with the guide.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus revenue ($123.3M) sits above the guide midpoint ($120M) by only about $3M, which is less than this award. If the market were confident the award was incremental and in Q3, consensus would have moved toward or above the top of the range. No analyst note dated after the award was found, and coverage is thin (HC Wainwright the only named estimate).
findings.independence: The Sep 14 2026 IR deck (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1367644/000136764426000091/hcw9-14x26ebs2026irconfe.htm) lists it as new in Q3, from the same issuer. The FY MCM guide is 'flat to slightly down', so it may already be inside guidance.

findings.finding: In Q3 Emergent repurchased $75M of its 3.875% 2028 unsecured notes for about $68M cash, roughly a 9% discount. Pro forma gross debt falls to $515M and cash to about $72M before Q3 operating cash flow. The result is a likely gain on extinguishment of about $7M plus about $2.9M a year of lower interest, all below operating income.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no clean prior: Q2 2026 carried a $20.5M loss on debt extinguishment from the OrbiMed term-loan refinancing, and the stock fell 29.6% on the guide cut, not on that line.
findings.why_not_priced: The deck was filed as a 7.01 exhibit and no wire story was found on it. A consensus EPS of -$0.40 to -$0.45 likely excludes a gain on extinguishment. If it were priced, the GAAP EPS estimates would show it. On financing: the money buys down the 2028 maturity at a discount, which is deleveraging, not distress. The cost is that cash falls to about $72M on a name with $40M of annual interest.

findings.finding: On 2026-08-31 the Government of Canada awarded Emergent a competitive standing offer to supply NARCAN Nasal Spray from 2026-10-01 to 2029-09-30, replacing the expiring five-year agreement. This retains an international naloxone channel that management could cite to firm the Commercial outlook (Q4 onward).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior reaction on this line is measurable; it is a renewal of an existing contract.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public and a renewal, so it is largely inside expectations. It is only worth something if management uses it to hold the FY Commercial guide of -20% to -25%. A loss of the tender would have been a visible negative, and that did not happen.

findings.finding: Q3 2026 is the first full quarter with Amphastar's Rextovy, a 4mg OTC naloxone approved 2026-06-16 and reportedly launched 2026-07-08, plus a 10mg prescription entrant launched in August. CDC provisional overdose deaths are down 12.3% year on year (12 months to March 2026), so Narcan volume and price could erode beyond the Aug 5 FY Commercial guide of -20% to -25%. Q2 naloxone was already $52.4M, down 22% year on year.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Naloxone erosion drove the Aug 5 2026 guide cut and the $191M NARCAN impairment: -29.6%. On Feb 26 2026 the FY2025 print with naloxone down 43% for the year moved -26.6%. This line has been sold hard each time it surprised negatively.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the Aug 5 guide was cut explicitly for these entrants, and the Sep 14 deck names them. What is not priced is the size of the first full-quarter impact; no channel data (IQVIA/Circana) on Narcan share since July was found. If the market had priced a further cut, the stock would not be +5% over 5 days and +14.5% since the last print (EW post-earnings drift).
findings.independence: This is a proxy, not a company number. The overdose-death trend comes from a different source: https://cdc.gov/overdose-prevention/data-research/facts-stats/index.html. Management's own Sep 14 deck says overdose deaths are falling faster than expected and pricing is more aggressive (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1367644/000136764426000091/hcw9-14x26ebs2026irconfe.htm). Net of the rest of the company: MCM (smallpox, anthrax, BAT) is the larger part of revenue and is contract-timed, so a naloxone miss can be offset by MCM deliveries.

findings.finding: The FY2026 guide (revenue $645-675M, adj. EBITDA $130-150M) against YTD revenue of $390.4M and YTD adj. EBITDA of $132M implies Q4 revenue of $125-175M, above the Q3 guide, and H2 adj. EBITDA of only $0-18M. The year therefore depends on Q4 MCM deliveries, and a reaffirmation is not a given on a name with eroding naloxone.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The FY guide has decided the last prints: a cut on Aug 5 2026 brought -29.6%; Q3 2025, when the guide was raised, brought +36.6% (baseline and the Aug 5 release).
findings.why_not_priced: This is arithmetic on public numbers, so the inputs are priced. The open question is the guide's direction on Nov 2, and the option market's 16.5% event move prices its size, not its sign.
findings.independence: This shares a document with the bar and is an inference rather than a new fact. It is separate from the naloxone finding (its driver is the timing of MCM deliveries), but if the guide is cut, both findings land on that one line.

findings.finding: CFO Richard Lindahl will retire on 2026-12-31. Treasurer Frank Vargo becomes interim CFO on 2027-01-01, not a permanent hire, during what the CEO called 'a critical juncture' in the turnaround.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior measurable reaction on this line.
findings.why_not_priced: It is already public. It matters only if the call ties the departure to the outlook; the 8-K neither reaffirmed nor changed guidance.

findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Positive reactions on this name have been very large: +36.6%, +36.7% and +34.2% in 2025. That is consistent with a short base covering into non-negative prints.
findings.why_not_priced: The baseline carries no short interest. A 16.5% event-implied move is below the name's own 29.6% median, which suggests the option market is not paying for the squeeze tail.

lessons_applied: Lesson 6, CYFENDUS: delivery quarter unknown and possibly inside FY MCM guidance; +1.0 trimmed to +0.8.
Lessons 2 and 4, bond buyback: below-the-line gain sized as a one-off; what the money buys is discounted deleveraging, so the sign stays positive; +0.5 to +0.3.
Lesson 6, Canada standing offer: a renewal inside expectations, moved toward 0; +0.5 to +0.2.
Naloxone erosion (lesson 5: proxy, not a company number; lesson 9: net of the larger MCM business; lesson 7: crowded short shrinks the negative): -1.5 to -0.8.
Lesson 7, back-half guide inference: crowded short shrinks the negative; -0.5 to -0.3.
Lesson 3, CFO change: no link to the outlook in the filing; -0.3 to -0.2.
Lesson 8: thin coverage and a 29.6% median own reaction, so abs_move_pct raised from 20 to 22 (option-implied 16.5).
Positioning (+1.0), insider sales (0.0) and the law-firm investigation (-0.1) left standing.
